mission: Approach across the cold mountain plateau and first entry into Gavran's Fortress. The building reads as geology until the angles give it away. The entry mechanism is calibrated for an older era than Ben's own training.
why_now: The coordinates land on this mountain; the wrongness is centered on this world. The fortress is why they came, and it has to be opened before the next level of the story can begin.
conflict: The Force-recognition mechanism scans Ben and almost refuses him — his modern Jedi training does not quite fit the signature the fortress was built to admit. Desh's tactical read is uncomplicated: defensible position, no extraction plan, the walls thicker than the weapons they have brought.
turning_point: The mechanism responds not to Ben's technique but to something older carried in his line. The amber hold goes green; the door concedes.
opening_hook: The fortress is built so precisely into the mountainside it reads as geology from the ridge — until Ben gets close enough to see that the angles are wrong.
closing_hook: The entry opens. Inside, the air has not moved for a thousand years. The wrongness here is concentrated and shaped — channeled through the mountain itself. Something is alive in here.
emotional_trajectory: Awed caution -> frustration with the lock -> unsettled recognition as it opens

stakes.personal: Ben is entering a tomb that has been sealed for a millennium
stakes.interpersonal: Desh's tactical assessment: defensible position, no extraction plan
stakes.external: Whatever the fortress contains is the source of the wrongness

setting: Uncharted world — cold mountain plateau, thin air, sharp light. Fortress exterior: weathered stone and metal alloy, no Jedi symbols visible
sensory_details: Thin atmosphere burning the lungs slightly; wind cutting across the plateau in continuous low registers; fortress stone carrying a thousand-year patina; the wrongness here arriving as a shaped weight — concentrated, directional, moving through the rock like a held breath
canon_elements_needed: Force-locked ancient Jedi facilities and bio-metric entry
Skywalker bloodline Force signature and hereditary recognition
Uncharted Outer Rim planetary environments and geology
Jedi Lords era fortress construction and defensive architecture
Thin place effects on Force-sensitive perception
action_beats: Ben and Desh trek across the thin-atmosphere plateau toward the fortress, breath steaming in the cold
Ben presses his palm against the entry mechanism — it resists, pulses amber, then recognizes his lineage and shifts to green
The fortress door grinds open, releasing sealed air that hasn't circulated in a thousand years
Desh sweeps the entry corridor with a glow rod while Ben reaches into the Force ahead of them
notes: The fortress should feel like a tomb before anyone says it is one. Environmental storytelling: the design reads urgency, permanence, and secrecy — no beauty, only endurance. Force phenomenology — rotate the wrongness metaphor for this chapter: not handrail, not note-played-flat. Here the register is weight and shape (held breath, pressure moving through rock). Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, articulate what the fortress is. He recognises the era from the construction without theorizing about who built it and why. Interpretation is the archive's job in the next scene. Anti-pattern: no Jedi symbols visible on the exterior — the building's secrecy is a fact of its design, not an aesthetic choice narrated by Ben.
